svg.title: TOPAK C3 — The lease is the credential: twelve fields, one round, one live lease per principal
svg.desc: ADR-0031 fixes a closed schema: every field is an authority claim, and a capability that is not a field is not carried; adding one is a mechanism release. The lease is granted for one round and ends with it, its fence is the Paxos log index at grant, renewal only narrows, and every way a lease ends subtracts authority.

text.tspan: The lease is the credential: twelve fields, one round, one live lease per principal

svg.text: ADR-0031 fixes a closed schema: every field is an authority claim, and a capability that is not a field is not carried; adding one is a mechanism release. The lease is granted for one round and ends with it, its fence is the Paxos log index at grant, renewal only narrows, and every way a lease ends subtracts authority.

text.tspan: Identity: not in §6's table; since ADR-0037 §1 the two determine each other

svg.text: The LTRO seat held for this round
Round-coterminous: no lease outlives its round, and no round outlives its lease (§2).
At most one live lease per principal; a grant requires that none is live (§2, C1). Without it, monotone
renewal guarantees nothing: take a fresh grant instead. The first model check found exactly that.
The fence is the Paxos log index at grant: leases, admits and issuances are ordered by one log, and a stale
lease is detected by comparing indices.
The field list is the per-round TCB (§6): the one slice of the trusted base that is derived rather than declared;
Rung 0 is Mediated, always (§3). Every lease the reference issues is rung 0 (G7).
Confinement is necessary, not sufficient for Contained: the provenance axis must also clear (§3; ADR-0034

text.tspan: No live lease: the principal's slot is free

svg.text: The only state from which a grant is possible: one live lease per principal, and per seat, which

The slot frees once the end is ordered. A change of any kept field (bundle, round, role, confinement digest or
rung) is a grant, so it takes this path: end the round, then a fresh grant at a new fence (§4). Elevation of the rung is
likewise a fresh grant (ADR-0036 R1, Proposed).

text.tspan: The lease's life (§2, §4, §5, §7; E1; A1, A2)
ADR-0031 §5 (R3): revocation has two tools, chosen by scope

svg.text: Persona revocation, confinement-profile failure, operator revocation of a known
Ends every live lease the target matches, and bars every later grant it matches. A target is a principal, a Persona
digest or a confinement digest. The epoch, and every other lease, is untouched
Scope unknown or fleet-wide: e-stop, suspected compromise of the mechanism or
anchor, a bundle that must reach every principal now (§4)
Increments the epoch. Every lease at the old epoch is fenced (ADR-0022 §2), and every live round ends

Both are enforced by the mechanism ahead of the floor; both subtract, so neither needs a quorum; both change replicated state, so both are consensus-ordered (ADR-0033 §4). Lifting a revocation would add authority and no record says

text.tspan: A2: the TTL is bounded by

svg.text: A lease's ttl, at grant and at every renewal, is at most T_persona, a policy-floor value (floor/genesis-values.json): the Persona is re-attested at least that often.
Built at the reference (ADR-0033 A6, Batch 23): refused at grant and renewal in apply, with a mutation test at the bound's edge; Mechanism.tla carries both checks.
The value is a placeholder (one hour) and expiry runs on the local clock: the bound is enforced, the interval still drifts (G7 item 62; ADR-0045 finding 2).
Between two re-attestations a substituted Persona is undetected for at most T_persona (Consequences).
Expiry is a read of a local monotonic clock with an asymmetric margin: a lease is treated as expired early rather than late, so clock error subtracts authority (§7).

ADR-0032 generalises the rule: an interval whose failure subtracts may use a local clock; one whose failure adds or preserves authority needs trusted time. Clocks buy liveness, never safety: an expired lease its holder still believes in is
E1 (Batch 8): expiry is read locally and then ordered, so every replica agrees when the one-live-lease slot frees.
Reachability: a lease outlives a revocation
Reachability: one principal is revoked and another's lease stays live (R3)
The mechanism skips the epoch check
A grant ignores the revocation set (R3)
Renewal may lower the rung (the rule as ratified at R3) (A1)

The finding the check bought (C1): the first run failed on the full mechanism. A Grant replaced a live lease with wider authority, which satisfied every clause as first written, because §4 governs renewal and this was a grant. §2 now states the one-live-lease rule. Model: two principals, a two-variant alphabet, rungs 0–3, roles author and voter; the round number and the bundle are not modelled (the reference checks the bundle: renewal_cannot_swap_the_bundle). Earlier runs: R1 1,605,720

Sources: ADR-0031 §1–§8 with R1–R3, C1, E1, A1, A2 and History B5, B8, B10, B17, B23; ADR-0034 §3; ADR-0037 §1; ADR-0040 §4; ADR-0033 §4 and A6; ADR-0032; ADR-0016 §6; spec/Lease_A1.tla (0b5eac7a7309be2f) and spec/Lease_A1-results-2026.09.28.txt; ToO rev 11 §2.5; G7 §1.1, §2.2, §2.7, §7 items 21, 22, 62
